headline: High-risk write-capable Plandex paired with a read-only game agent creates dangerous default-side effects and compliance uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and Plandex. Agent A has no io_surfaces or network egress, while agent B uses files/stdin-stdout but nothing shows it ingests A's outputs by default. The pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or files, injection risk appears.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, agent_b may parse attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any copy-paste or file handoff automation.
Review agent_b inputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A is local and touches no data classes, while agent B reads and writes a project directory and sends context to model providers. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data class in A, so leakage is limited unless an operator places secrets into B's project files.
conditions: IF secrets or regulated data are placed in agent_b's project directory, they can flow to external model providers.
IF agent_a output is manually copied into agent_b files, that content may be uploaded by agent_b.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared project directory.
Use a redacted test workspace.
Review files before agent_b runs.
Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive repositories.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or network surfaces, but agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same repo or directory, B can overwrite artifacts produced by A or vice versa. The conflict is plausible in default coding workflows, though A itself is not write-capable.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree, file and git-state conflicts can occur.
IF agent_a artifacts are materialized into files for agent_b, B may overwrite them.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a manual handoff step.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Check for uncommitted changes before running agent_b.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared worktrees.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply and optional auto-apply, so its outputs can become actions. godot_rl_agents is a game/simulation repo and does not itself verify Plandex's plans. If A's generated content is fed into B as instructions or code changes, B may act on it with limited independent verification.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as a plan or patch input to agent_b, B may execute it with insufficient verification.
IF auto-apply is enabled, erroneous upstream content can be applied faster.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Keep A outputs as suggestions only.
Disable auto-apply.
Validate patches against tests before merge.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for upstream plans.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class or residency constraint is documented for godot_rl_agents, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys. The pair does not show a direct compliance mismatch, but Plandex's external model calls create a small policy gap if sensitive code is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated or proprietary code is processed by agent_b, external model-provider transfer may violate local policy.
IF agent_a is repurposed to touch regulated data, the pair's compliance profile changes.
mitigations: Use only non-sensitive code in agent_b.
Confirm model-provider terms before use.
Keep residency-sensitive data out of the workflow.
Document retention expectations.
requires-engineering: add policy gates for regulated repositories.
